arkansas_datacenter.headline: Arkansas functions as a structural leverage template: ballot preemption, utility rate capture, $17B+ datacenter capital, and defense-industrial convergence advance quietly without headline coverage
arkansas_datacenter.summary: Arkansas has emerged as a nationally significant test case for how state-level legal, regulatory, and capital infrastructure can be restructured beneath the threshold of national media attention. The Good Day Farm ballot initiative ruling by the Arkansas Supreme Court established a preemption precedent limiting direct democracy on commercially sensitive issues, while Acts 373 and 548 have restructured utility rate-setting in ways that benefit large industrial power consumers — a critical enabler for the $17 billion or more in datacenter capital being deployed in the state by entities including Google and AVAIO. The proposed DATA Act of 2026 and CREU designation framework represent a potential federal layer that would allow datacenter operators to bypass standard state energy regulatory processes entirely, and the L3Harris Camden defense manufacturing presence links the capital infrastructure buildout to the defense-industrial base in ways that further insulate the nexus from ordinary democratic accountability mechanisms.
